title: Hierarchical prefix collapse and eviction profiles for GPU KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current per-prefix fragment store produces many small, near-duplicate fragments across requests (same prompt header variations, templated slots, small metadata differences). These fragments bloat GPU-resident KV, causing lower effective cache hit rates and forcing more frequent slab eviction which increases tail latency and token cost.

Goal: Reduce GPU KV footprint and increase cross-request prefix reuse by collapsing similar prefixes into a compact hierarchical index and applying slab-aware eviction profiles so hot fragments remain resident and low-value duplicates are deduplicated. Target: 20–30% reduction in GPU KV memory for high-mix workloads and a 10%+ improvement in end-to-end token throughput for typical conversational traces without increasing 95th percentile latency by >5ms.

Proposal summary:
1) Build a lightweight hierarchical prefix canonicalization step that maps syntactically-similar prefix variants to a normalized signature at ingest time. The hierarchy has 3 levels: exact-hash, structural-signature (slot-normalized), and semantic-fingerprint (fast LSH-style sketch).
2) Maintain a synthetic prefix index (compact in CPU memory) that points to slab-resident fragment groups, allowing fast lookups across requests for potential reuse. The index stores: canonical_signature -> [slab_id, fragment_ref_count, last_access_ts, hotspot_score].
3) Introduce slab-aware eviction profiles: each slab maintains an eviction priority which accounts for group hotspot_score and expected reuse. Eviction moves low-priority fragments to a small spill buffer (CPU or NVMe) rather than immediate free, allowing opportunistic rehydration when similar requests arrive.
4) GPU locality hints: allocate newly-coalesced prefix groups preferentially to slabs that already contain related fragments to minimize cross-slab fragmentation and reduce expensive memory compaction.

Trade-offs and risks:
- CPU overhead for canonicalization and index maintenance. We'll mitigate by batching canonicalization and using SIMD-friendly normalization rules.
- False-positive merges (over-aggressive collapse) can reduce quality/hit correctness for some workloads; we will start with conservative structural rules and gated semantic thresholds.
- Interference across tenants: canonicalization must respect tenant isolation; index entries are tenant-scoped to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Success metrics:
- GPU KV resident bytes per active session (median + 95th).
- Fragment count and average fragment size.
- Cache hit ratio (prefix-lookup hits) and end-to-end token cost per request.
- 95th percentile generation latency and tail latency contribution from cache misses.

Out-of-scope for initial rollouts: cross-region shared index, automatic semantic merging using expensive models (deferred to future work).

Implementation plan (phases):
A. Prototype (2 sprints): CPU-only canonicalizer + synthetic index emulator; replay production traces to validate collapse effectiveness and false-positive rates.
B. Integration (1 sprint): integrate index into KV write path with optional feature flag; implement slab-aware eviction metadata.
C. GPU allocation + locality hints (1 sprint): modify allocator to prefer co-located slabs and add spill buffer path.
D. Canary + measurement (2 weeks): gated rollout behind canary; collect metrics and compare against baseline traces.

Observability and telemetry: add metrics for canonicalization rate, collisions, index lookup latency, spill buffer usage, slab hotspot distribution, and per-tenant memory savings. Create dashboard templates in Console under project "kv-reuse-and-footprint-optimization".

Rollout strategy: feature-flagged default-off. Start with internal canaries on low-traffic tenants, then opt-in beta customers, then automated canary with rollback if GC or latency regressions detected.

Documentation and artifacts: Confluence design doc and benchmark playbook, GitHub PRs with perf microbenchmarks, and a rollout checklist with SLO thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Synthetic index reduces distinct GPU-resident fragment count by >=20% on replay traces. 2) End-to-end generation cost per token reduces by >=8% on test batch without >5ms on p95 latency. 3) No cross-tenant index leakage and security checks pass. 4) Telemetry dashboards show canonicalization hit/miss and spill buffer events. 5) Code merged behind feature flag and canary rollout plan exists.
implementation_notes:
- Keep canonicalizer implementation packaged so it can be toggled per-deployment (hosted vs dedicated).
- Use SIMD-friendly normalization (strip numeric IDs, normalize whitespace, collapse common template tokens).
- Synthetic index must be compact; store 64-bit signature + 32-bit slab_id + small metadata.
- Spill buffer path will reuse existing CPU-backed KV spill interface (see ENG-12859).
- Add per-tenant quotas for index entries to avoid unbounded growth.
- Bench harness: replay trace from 2026-02 prod sample (s3://infra-prod-traces/2026-02-sample) and run on small 4-GPU cluster to measure wall-time and memory footprint.
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Initial triage and writeup. Observed high duplicate-fragment ratios in prod trace: ~35% of fragments had >80% commonality with other fragments. Raised as high-impact for GPU resident memory growth.

2026-02-24 Marco Ruiz: Added prototype canonicalizer. Early replay shows 18% fragment reduction with conservative structural rules. CPU overhead measured ~6% of single-core load in microbench; still acceptable for batch processing.
2026-03-02 Design review (Sana Kim): Recommended conservative default thresholds and explicit tenant isolation. Suggested adding spill buffer instead of immediate eviction to reduce miss penalty.

2026-03-05 Perf run (internal canary): On 4-GPU small cluster, synthetic index reduced resident fragment bytes by 22% and improved token throughput by 11% on conversational trace. Noted small increase in canonicalizer CPU usage during ingest spikes.
2026-03-09 Code review (PR #5109): Engineering feedback: tighten memory accounting for index to prevent double-counting with slab allocator. Marco to address in follow-up commit.

2026-03-12 Marco Ruiz: Addressed accounting bug and added per-tenant entry cap. Preparing canary rollout plan and Grafana dashboards. Next: enable internal canaries and collect 1 week of telemetry before wider beta.
